claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC and dendritic.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 800 MPa at room temperature.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding a minor amount of yttrium during processing can promote in situ formation of Y2O3 or other Y-rich oxide nanoparticles in TiVNbTa.
The intervention will produce a fine, uniformly distributed dispersion of Y-rich oxide particles within the BCC matrix.
The Y-rich oxide particles will remain thermally stable near 1273 K.
Y-rich oxide particles will hinder dislocation motion in TiVNbTa.
Y-rich oxide particles will stabilize or pin grain boundaries in TiVNbTa.
Grain-boundary stabilization will reduce grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Reduced dislocation mobility and grain-boundary sliding will mitigate thermal softening and creep.
The oxide-modified alloy will have a statistically significant increase in yield strength at 1273 K relative to the approximately 330 MPa baseline.
The oxide-modified alloy will maintain adequate ductility at 1273 K.
The intervention is applicable at temperatures up to 1273 K and strains of approximately 30–40%.
The intervention can improve strength without compromising the thermal conductivity needed to transfer heat between W and CuCrZr.
